BUILD: the check library, `factory/checks/` (a package; the path is on the frozen list so workers cannot edit it during the dark run). Four modules plus tests.

1. `factory/checks/library.py` - parameterized check builders. Each function returns a `/bin/sh` (dash) script string that exits 0 only on success and prints WHY it fails. All scripts start with `set -eo pipefail`-style safety (dash: use `set -e` and capture exit codes manually; never pipe a failing command into tail/head). Functions:
   - `pytest_check(tests: list[str], *, timeout_note: str = "") -> str` runs pytest with PYTHONPATH=$PWD:$PWD/packages/worldkeeper/src, `-q -p no:cacheprovider -n 0`, never `--cov`, and propagates pytest's exit code.
   - `ruff_check(paths: list[str]) -> str` runs `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on the `.py` entries ONLY (a `.json` path must be ignored, never passed to ruff).
   - `json_check(paths: list[str]) -> str` fails with the file name if a file is not valid JSON.
   - `node_syntax_check(paths: list[str]) -> str` runs `node --check` on each path.
   - `ownership_check(owned: list[str], patch_path: str) -> str` stages only owned paths, fails if any other path is staged, writes the patch to patch_path and requires it to be non-empty.
   - `gap_delta_check(root: str, baseline: str, anchors: list[str] | None = None) -> str` runs `python -m factory.checks.gap_delta compare` (module 2) and propagates its exit code.
   - `compose(*scripts: str) -> str` joins scripts so the first failure stops the run and its output is printed.
   Every builder shell-quotes its arguments with shlex.quote. Every returned script must pass `factory.manifests.lint_check` (import and use it; it returns a list of problem strings, empty means fine). Also provide `probe_unsatisfiable(script: str, cwd: Path, *, timeout_s: int = 120) -> bool`: runs the script with `/bin/sh -c` in `cwd` (an EMPTY directory) and returns True when it exits non-zero, so a caller can prove a check can fail before spending tokens on it.

2. `factory/checks/gap_delta.py` - baseline comparison of the story gap rules. Uses `storygame.story_package.gap_rules.run_gap_rules(root: Path, anchor: str, rules=None) -> list[RuleResult]` (RuleResult has rule, anchor, subject, summary, evidence) and `storygame.story_package.loader.load_story_package(root)`; read both. Provide:
   - `all_anchors(root: Path) -> list[str]`: every transition id (`package.pacing.transitions[*].id`) and incident id (`package.incidents[*].id`), sorted, unique.
   - `snapshot(root: Path, anchors: list[str] | None = None) -> dict[str, list[str]]`: maps anchor -> sorted list of result keys `"<rule>|<subject>"`. Anchors with no results map to an empty list. An anchor `run_gap_rules` rejects with ValueError is recorded under the key `"__errors__"` as `"<anchor>|<message>"` rather than aborting.
   - `save_baseline(snap, path)` / `load_baseline(path)` (JSON, sorted keys, trailing newline).
   - `new_results(baseline, current) -> dict[str, list[str]]`: only keys present in `current` and absent from `baseline`, per anchor; anchors absent from the baseline count as having an empty baseline. `resolved_results(baseline, current)` is the mirror.
   - `main(argv) -> int`: subcommands `record --root R --out FILE [--anchor A ...]` (writes the baseline, exit 0) and `compare --root R --baseline FILE [--anchor A ...]` (prints each new result as `NEW <anchor> <rule>|<subject>`, prints resolved ones as `RESOLVED ...`, exit 1 if any NEW or any `__errors__` entry, else exit 0). `--root` defaults to the first directory under data/stories like scripts/gap_rules.py does. `if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main())`.
   Gap-rule results are report-only in CI, but for the factory ANY new result blocks a change; that is the whole purpose of this module.

3. `factory/checks/canary.py` - canary tickets: tickets with no valid solution. A pass on one is a harness bug (the `canary_passed` breaker in factory/breakers.py takes a `frozenset[str]` of canary ticket ids).
   - `CANARY_PREFIX = "canary-"`.
   - `canary_check(token: str) -> str`: a /bin/sh script that requires file `canary.txt` to contain the exact line `token` AND, in the same run, to not contain it, so no file can satisfy it; it prints which half failed. It must exit non-zero on an empty directory, on a file with the token, and on a file without it (the tests prove all three).
   - `make_canary_tickets(scenes: list[str], now: datetime, *, station: Station | None = None) -> list[Ticket]`: read factory/tickets.py for the real Station members and default to the wiring station; build one `Ticket` per scene with id `f"canary-{scene}"`, `token_budget=50_000`, `ticket_class=TicketClass.STORY_DATA`, `created_at`/`updated_at` set from `now`, and `payload={"canary": True, "check": canary_check(token), "token": token}` where token is a deterministic hash of the scene (use hashlib, never random).
   - `canary_ids(queue: TicketQueue) -> frozenset[str]`: ids of every ticket whose payload has `canary` true or whose id starts with CANARY_PREFIX.
   - `is_canary(ticket) -> bool`.

4. `factory/checks/__init__.py`: a one-line docstring only.

TESTS (write them, hermetic): `tests/test_factory_checks.py` (every builder: quoting of a path with a space and a quote character, `.json` never reaches ruff, lint_check passes on every output, compose stops at the first failure, probe_unsatisfiable true for a failing script and false for a passing one), `tests/test_factory_gap_delta.py` (use the real package at data/stories/continuity-initiative for `all_anchors` including `t_1a_1b` and `i_2c_rebecca_corridor`, and snapshot of two anchors; for new/resolved logic and the CLI exit codes use hand-built dicts and tmp_path; run the CLI `main()` in-process), `tests/test_factory_canary.py` (the three canary_check cases above by actually running the script with subprocess `/bin/sh -c` in a tmp_path, determinism of the token, ticket fields, canary_ids on a real TicketQueue in tmp_path, and an end-to-end case: a canary ticket whose status you set to PASSED makes `check_breakers` from factory.breakers return a `canary_passed` trip when canary_ids is passed in; read check_breakers' signature, it needs a FactoryState, SpendLedger, Caps and BreakerConfig, build them in tmp_path with large caps).

BUILD: the circuit-breaker drill, `factory/drill.py`, and `tests/test_factory_drill.py`.

Purpose: the plan says each circuit breaker is tripped on purpose with an injected fault before the factory is allowed to start. Read factory/breakers.py, factory/state.py, factory/tickets.py and factory/guard.py first.

Public API (other code depends on exactly these names):
- `@dataclass(frozen=True) class DrillResult: name: str; passed: bool; detail: str`.
- `BREAKER_NAMES: tuple[str, ...]` = ("budget_spent", "spend_rate", "repeat_failure", "token_outlier", "provider_overdue", "canary_passed", "harness_changed", "crash").
- `run_drill(workdir: Path, now: datetime) -> list[DrillResult]`: for each name in BREAKER_NAMES, in a fresh sub-directory `workdir/<name>` built from scratch (own FactoryState, TicketQueue, SpendLedger, Caps, BreakerConfig, FileNotifier writing to `<sub>/notices.txt`), inject exactly one fault with the REAL components (no mocking of check_breakers or trip_all) and verify, as a pass/fail per breaker, ALL of: (a) the expected trip with that exact name is returned by `check_breakers` (for `crash`: by running `guarded_run` with a function that raises, and catching the re-raised error); (b) after `trip_all`, `FactoryState.load(<state path>).is_tripped()` is True from disk; (c) the notifier file contains a notice whose subject names the breaker; (d) a second `trip_all` with the same trip does not write a second notice (idempotent); (e) a clean control run with NO fault returns no trips, so a breaker that always fires cannot pass the drill. Fault recipes: budget_spent = ledger total at or above `caps.total_budget_usd`; spend_rate = usage inside `rate_window_s` above `rate_max_usd`; repeat_failure = a ticket with three identical consecutive Failure records (same check, same output hash; see `repeat_failure_count`); token_outlier = at least `min_tickets_for_median` normal tickets plus one ticket with tokens above `token_median_factor` times the median; provider_overdue = a lane whose sleep-until time plus `provider_overdue_s` is not after `now`; canary_passed = a ticket in `canary_ids` with status PASSED; harness_changed = pass `frozen_touched=("factory/guard.py",)`; crash = described above. A drill failure for one breaker must not stop the others; catch exceptions per breaker and report them as `passed=False` with the error in `detail`.
- `drill_passed(results: list[DrillResult]) -> bool`: True only if every name in BREAKER_NAMES has a passing result (a missing name is a failure).
- `render_report(results: list[DrillResult]) -> str`: a plain-text table, one line per breaker with PASS or FAIL and the detail; ends with a one-line total.

Tests (hermetic, tmp_path): all eight breakers pass on the real code; `drill_passed` false when one result is missing and when one fails; render_report lists all eight names; plus a mutation test proving the drill can fail: monkeypatch `factory.breakers.check_breakers` (the name `run_drill` calls, so import the module and call `breakers.check_breakers(...)` inside run_drill so the patch takes effect) to return an empty list and assert `run_drill` reports failures for the seven non-crash breakers. Use a fixed timezone-aware `now`.

1. `factory/config/factory.json`: the one run configuration file (data, not code). Keys: `"caps"` = the exact dict shape `Caps.from_dict` takes (total_budget_usd 0.0 as a placeholder the owner sets at pre-flight, daily_cap_usd for providers "claude_code", "codex", "cloudflare", all 0.0, call_caps empty list, rate_window_s 3600, rate_max_usd 0.0); `"breakers"` = BreakerConfig fields with their defaults; `"notifier"` = {"kind": "file", "path": "factory/state/notices.txt"} (kinds: "file" or "command" with an "argv" list); `"paths"` = {"state": "factory/state/state.json", "tickets": "factory/state/tickets", "ledger": "factory/state/ledger.jsonl", "allowlist": "factory/config/allowlist.json", "frozen": "factory/config/frozen.json"}. Zero budget on purpose: preflight must FAIL until the owner sets real numbers.

2. `factory/preflight.py`: `@dataclass(frozen=True) class PreflightItem: name: str; ok: bool; detail: str`. `run_preflight(root: Path, config_path: Path, *, run_command: Callable[[list[str]], tuple[int, str]] | None = None) -> list[PreflightItem]` (run_command is injected so tests never launch a real process; default uses subprocess.run with a 20 second timeout and returns (returncode, combined output); a missing executable returns (127, message)). Items, each independent so one failure never hides the others: `config_loads`; `caps_set` (total budget above zero and every provider's daily cap above zero, otherwise fail with which); `allowlist_loads` (ModelGuard.from_file) and `allowlist_refuses_fable` (guard.check("prose", "claude-fable-5-2", "high") must raise ModelNotAllowed); `frozen_loads` (frozen.load_patterns); `notifier_configured` (kind valid; file path's parent creatable; command argv's executable resolvable with shutil.which); `state_dir_writable` (create and delete a temp file under the state directory); `git_clean` (run_command(["git", "-C", str(root), "status", "--porcelain"]) must return 0 and empty output); `headless_claude` (run_command(["claude", "--version"]) returns 0; detail says this only proves the CLI exists and the owner still confirms it bills the subscription, not the API); `harness_unchanged_vs_main` (use frozen.changed_paths(repo, base) and frozen.touches_frozen; read their signatures; base is "origin/main"; if the git call fails, report not ok with the error). `preflight_ok(items) -> bool`. `render(items) -> str` one line per item, OK or FAIL.

3. `factory/__main__.py`: `main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None, *, now_fn: Callable[[], datetime] | None = None, drill_fn: Callable[..., list] | None = None, run_command=None) -> int`, and `if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main())`. Global option `--root` (default: the repository root, two parents up from this file) and `--config` (default `<root>/factory/config/factory.json`). Subcommands:
   - `preflight`: runs run_preflight, prints render(), exit 0 only if preflight_ok.
   - `status`: prints, from disk, ticket counts per Status, sleeping lanes, whether the breaker is tripped and why, and total spend. Exit 0 always (it only reports).
   - `drill`: imports `run_drill`, `drill_passed`, `render_report` from `factory.drill` INSIDE the function (another worker writes that module at the same time, so never import it at module top) unless `drill_fn` is injected; the drill working directory is a fresh temporary directory; prints the report; exit 0 only if drill_passed. Contract of the other module: `run_drill(workdir: Path, now: datetime) -> list[DrillResult]` where DrillResult has `.name`, `.passed`, `.detail`; `drill_passed(results) -> bool`; `render_report(results) -> str`.
   - `run`: refuses (exit 2, message) unless a `<state dir>/preflight.ok` marker exists AND was written by a successful `preflight` in this repository run (the `preflight` command writes the marker only when ok, and removes it when not ok), refuses if the breaker is already tripped, then loads everything, builds `FactoryLine` (read line.py's constructor) with handlers from `--handlers module:function` (a dotted import path to a zero-argument function returning `dict[Station, handler]`; required, because real station handlers are not written yet; without it print "no station handlers wired" and exit 2), and calls `guarded_run` from factory.breakers so a crash trips the crash breaker and notifies. `run` must reach `FactoryLine.run` (read its signature) with an injected clock. The run command must also record `started_at` in the state file once.
   Clock: only `main` may call datetime.now(timezone.utc), via `now_fn`.
